g.text: A brief uses the modules it needs.
Not every brief uses every module.
MAKE is a set of modules, not one product you switch on whole. The same platform serves a single-asset request and a nine-market campaign, with nothing to re-implement in between.
Each module serves a different part of the production
A module is switched on for a brief or it is not. There is no
partial state, no separate implementation, and no second
Four of the eight are named below. The rest are named in
our existing deck and are carried here as placeholders.
Full campaign, nine markets, every format
E‑commerce refresh across a product range
Complexity is only a problem if you have to absorb all of it.
Brief A touches two modules. Nobody on your side configures, licences or
learns the other six. The system scales up to Brief B without a second implementation, and back down again without a decommission.
Modules 2 to 5 are unnamed here on purpose.
They are the five-step set that already exists in our current deck, and their
names did not come up in the discussion. The current product playbook was reviewed and is out of date, so it is not a usable source.
These names are the client’s mental model of the product.
This slide cannot go into the submission until they are confirmed.
